license: fair-code: sustainable use license, NOT osi open source

steps.label: docker
steps.cmd: apt-get update && apt-get install -y docker.io docker-compose-v2

steps.label: up
steps.cmd: docker rm -f spawnables-n8n >/dev/null 2>&1; docker run -d --restart unless-stopped --name spawnables-n8n -p 5678:5678 -v /opt/spawnables-services/n8n:/home/node/.n8n docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:latest

notes: workflow automation, 400+ integrations, self-hosted. the license is the honest part: n8n is fair-code (sustainable use license), source-available but not osi-approved, and reselling it as a service is restricted. fine for an owner-run machine, worth knowing before anyone builds a product on it. workflows and credentials live in the volume, so freeze/thaw carries them.
